lessons.title: How Excel stores dates and times
learn: Serial numbers, why dates show as numbers
The 1904 date system on old Mac files
lessons.mac:
the 1904 date system
Very old Mac workbooks may count days from 1-Jan-1904.
Dates copied between a 1900 file and a 1904 file shift by 4 years and 1 day (1,462 days).
Check it in the Excel app on Mac: Excel menu > Preferences > Calculation > Use the 1904 date system.

steps.say: On the finished sheet, the same dates and times are shown the way Excel really stores them: whole numbers for dates and fractions of a day for times. Once you see this, date maths makes sense.
Here's the plan for this lesson.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Dates are serial numbers, times are fractions
• Why a date sometimes shows as a number
• Adding days to a date
• The 1904 date system on old Mac files
Practice sheet: S06-01

steps.say: Excel counts days from the first of January 1900, which is day 1. Every date is just the number of days since then. A time is a fraction of a day, so noon is 0.5.

acts.t:
Dates = whole numbers counted from 1-Jan-1900 (day 1)
01-04-2026 = 46113
Times = fractions of a day: 06:00 = 0.25, 12:00 = 0.5, 18:00 = 0.75
Date and time together = whole number + fraction

steps.say: Open sheet S06-01. Column C holds exactly the same dates and times as column B. Select C2 to C11.
On the Home tab, open the Number Format box and choose General.
Each date becomes a plain number. The first of April 2026 is 46113, that many days since the start of 1900. Excel's day one, in row 6, is simply 1.
The times became fractions. Noon is 0.5, half a day, and six in the evening is 0.75. Half past nine is a longer decimal, because nine and a half hours is not a round fraction of twenty-four.
Because dates are numbers, you can add days to them. In D2, type equals B2 plus 30, press Return and fill down to D5. The first of April plus thirty days is the first of May.

acts.h: Select D2:D5 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: This is also why a date sometimes appears as a number. Select D2 to D5 and set the format to General. The due dates turn into numbers like 46143. Nothing is broken; only the format changed.
Press Command Z to undo, and the dates are back. If a date column ever shows five-digit numbers, change the format, not the data.
A word on typing dates. Excel reads what you type using your regional settings.

acts.t:
Typing dates
With Indian settings (English, India), 15-08-2026 is read as 15 August 2026.
With US settings, it may stay as text.
Year-month-day, like 2026-08-15, is understood with any setting.

steps.say: Let's prove that. Click B2 and type 2026-04-10, in year-month-day form, then press Return. The cell shows the tenth of April, and the date in D2 moves to the tenth of May.
One thing that only matters on a Mac.

acts.t:
Mac corner: the 1904 date system
Very old Mac workbooks may count days from 1-Jan-1904.
Dates copied between a 1900 file and a 1904 file shift by 4 years and 1 day (1,462 days).
Check it in the Excel app on Mac: Excel menu > Preferences > Calculation > Use the 1904 date system.

steps.say: Here's a quick recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• A date is a count of days; a time is a fraction of a day
• A date showing as 46113 just needs a date format
• Add whole numbers to move dates by days

steps.say: Your turn. In G2, find the serial number for the first of January 2026. Use DATE of 2026, 1, 1 and format the cell as General.

acts.t:
Challenge
In G2, show the serial number of 1 January 2026.
Hint: =DATE(2026,1,1), then format as General
Answer: sheet S06-01 Done

lessons.title: TODAY, NOW, DATE and the date parts
learn: Build a date from separate columns
lessons.mac:
(Excel app on Mac)
Control + ; types today's date as a fixed value
Command + ; types the current time as a fixed value
Unlike TODAY() and NOW(), these never change

steps.say: Here, every joining date is broken into year, month and day, today's date and time update on their own, and dates exported as three separate columns are rebuilt into real dates.
Here's the plan for this lesson.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• TODAY and NOW
• YEAR, MONTH, DAY, HOUR and MINUTE
• DATE: build a date from separate columns
Practice sheet: S06-02

steps.say: TODAY and NOW take no arguments. YEAR, MONTH and DAY pull parts out of a date, and HOUR and MINUTE do the same for a time. DATE goes the other way and always takes the year first.

acts.t:
TODAY()  today's date      NOW()  date and time
YEAR(date)  MONTH(date)  DAY(date)
HOUR(time)  MINUTE(time)
DATE(year, month, day)  year first, always

steps.say: Open sheet S06-02. Column B has joining dates, and HR wants the year, month and day in separate columns. Click C2.
Type equals YEAR of B2, press Return and fill down to C9 with Command D.

acts.h: Select C2:C9 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: In D2, type equals MONTH of B2 and fill down. Months come back as numbers from 1 to 12.

acts.h: Select D2:D9 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: In E2, type equals DAY of B2 and fill down. Aditi joined on the fifteenth.

acts.h: Select E2:E9 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Now the live functions. In I1, type equals TODAY, open and close brackets, and press Return. It shows today's date and updates whenever the file recalculates.
In I2, type equals NOW with empty brackets. NOW gives the date and the current time.
HOUR and MINUTE pull the time apart. In I3, type HOUR of I2, and in I4, type MINUTE of I2.
Now the opposite job. Many HR and bank systems export the year, month and day in separate columns. In D13, type equals DATE of A13, B13, C13, press Return and fill down to D16.

acts.h: Select D13:D16 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Row 16 asks for the thirtieth of February 2026, which doesn't exist. DATE rolls the extra days into March and returns the second of March. Useful for maths, but worth checking in imported data.

In India we write the day first, so a common slip is giving DATE the day first too. Retype D13 as DATE of C13, B13, A13 and press Return. You get a date in 1906, because DATE always reads the year first.
Put it back in year, month, day order and press Return.
The parts follow the source. Aditi's joining date was corrected to the twentieth of May 2024. In B2, type 2024-05-20 and press Return. Year, month and day update together.
One shortcut to know on a Mac.

acts.t:
Mac corner (Excel app on Mac)
Control + ; types today's date as a fixed value
Command + ; types the current time as a fixed value
Unlike TODAY() and NOW(), these never change

steps.say: Here's a quick recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• TODAY() and NOW() update on their own; use them for 'as of now' cells
• YEAR, MONTH, DAY, HOUR, MINUTE pull parts out
• DATE(year, month, day) builds a real date, year first

steps.say: Your turn. In column F, show the full month name of each joining date, such as April, using TEXT with the code mmmm.

acts.t:
Challenge
In F2:F9, show the month name of the joining date, e.g. April.
Hint: TEXT(B2, "mmmm")
Answer: sheet S06-02 Done

steps.say: This contract tracker shows each renewal date, the last day of the start month and the invoice due date at the end of the next month. All of it handles short months and leap years correctly.
Here's the plan for this lesson.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• EDATE: the same day, some months later or earlier
• EOMONTH: the last day of a month
• Why adding 30 days is not a month
Practice sheet: S06-03

steps.say: EDATE moves a date by whole months. EOMONTH jumps to the last day of a month, where zero means the same month, 1 the next month, and minus 1 the month before.

acts.t:
EDATE(start_date, months)  e.g. EDATE(B2, 12) = one year later
EOMONTH(start_date, months)  last day of that month
months: 0 = same month, 1 = next, -1 = previous

steps.say: Open sheet S06-03. Each contract has a start date and a term in months. Click D2 for the renewal date.

A tempting shortcut is thirty days per month. Type equals B2 plus C2 times 30 and press Return. Twelve months from the thirty-first of January 2026 comes out as the twenty-sixth of January 2027. Months aren't all thirty days.
EDATE adds whole months. Retype D2 as equals EDATE of B2, comma, C2, and press Return. Now it's the thirty-first of January 2027, exactly twelve months on.
Fill down. Look at Security services in row 6. One month after the thirty-first of January is the twenty-eighth of February. EDATE stops at the last valid day instead of spilling into March.

acts.h: Select D2:D9 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: If a result ever shows as a five-digit number, the cell is in General format. Choose Short Date or a date format from the Number Format box on the Home tab.
EOMONTH gives the last day of a month. In E2, type equals EOMONTH of B2, comma, 0. Zero means the same month. Fill down.

acts.h: Select E2:E9 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Many vendors are paid at the end of the following month. In F2, type EOMONTH of B2, comma, 1, which gives the last day of the next month. Fill down.

acts.h: Select F2:F9 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Here's a pro tip for the first day of a month.

acts.t:
Pro tip
First day of the month: =EOMONTH(B2,-1)+1
Last day of the previous month, plus one day

steps.say: Now change an input. The generator rental was extended to three months. Type 3 in C9 and press Return. The renewal date moves to the thirty-first of March 2026.
Here's a quick recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• EDATE(date, months) for renewals, EMIs and due dates
• EOMONTH(date, 0) is month end; 1 is next month end
• Never add 30 for a month; short months will catch you

steps.say: Your turn. In column G, set a reminder one month before each renewal date. Use EDATE with a negative number.

acts.t:
Challenge
In G2:G9, show the date one month before the renewal date in column D.
Hint: EDATE(D2, -1)
Answer: sheet S06-03 Done

steps.say: For two weeks of April 2026, this sheet shows each day's name, its weekday number, whether it's a working day and its week number for the weekly report.
Here's the plan for this lesson.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Day names with TEXT
• WEEKDAY and its return type
• Weekend flags with IF
• Week numbers with WEEKNUM
Practice sheet: S06-04

steps.say: WEEKDAY returns the day as a number, and the second argument decides where the week starts. With return type 2, Monday is 1 and Sunday is 7. WEEKNUM returns the week of the year.

acts.t:
TEXT(date, "dddd")  Monday, Tuesday...
WEEKDAY(date, [return_type])
  1 or blank: Sunday = 1 ... Saturday = 7
  2: Monday = 1 ... Sunday = 7
WEEKNUM(date, [return_type])  2 = weeks start Monday

steps.say: Open sheet S06-04. Column A has the first fourteen days of April 2026. Click B2.
Type equals TEXT of A2, comma, dddd in quotes, press Return and fill down. The first of April 2026 is a Wednesday.

acts.h: Select B2:B15 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: WEEKDAY gives the day as a number. In C2, type equals WEEKDAY of A2 with no second argument, and fill down. Wednesday shows 4, because by default the week starts on Sunday.

acts.h: Select C2:C15 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Now flag weekends. In D2, type IF of WEEKDAY of A2 greater than 5, Weekend, otherwise Working day. Fill down.

acts.h: Select D2:D15 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Look closely. Friday the third is marked Weekend and Sunday the fifth is a Working day. With Sunday as day 1, the numbers above 5 are Friday and Saturday.
The fix is the second argument. Return type 2 numbers Monday as 1 and Sunday as 7, so only Saturday and Sunday are above 5. Retype C2 with comma 2 and fill down.

acts.h: Select C2:C15 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Retype D2 with WEEKDAY of A2, comma 2, and fill down. Now only Saturdays and Sundays are weekends.

acts.h: Select D2:D15 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: For weekly reports, WEEKNUM gives the week number. In E2, type equals WEEKNUM of A2, comma, 2, so weeks start on Monday. Fill down. The first of April is in week 14, and the number changes on Monday the sixth.

acts.h: Select E2:E15 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: If you work with international teams, there's a second week system.

acts.t:
Pro tip
ISOWEEKNUM(date) gives the ISO week, where week 1 is the week containing the first Thursday of the year.
Many European and global companies report by ISO week.

steps.say: Change the first date to see everything follow. Type 2026-03-29 in A2 and press Return. Row 2 becomes Sunday, a weekend.
Here's a quick recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• TEXT(date,"dddd") gives the day name
• Use WEEKDAY(date, 2): Monday 1 to Sunday 7, weekend is > 5
• WEEKNUM(date, 2) for Monday-start week numbers

steps.say: Your turn. In column F, show the short day name, such as Wed, using TEXT with three d's.

acts.t:
Challenge
In F2:F15, show the short day name, e.g. Wed.
Hint: TEXT(A2, "ddd")
Answer: sheet S06-04 Done

lessons.title: WORKDAY and NETWORKDAYS with Indian holidays

steps.say: This purchase order tracker counts working days between order and promise, for a five-day and a six-day week, and works out delivery dates that skip weekends and holidays.
Here's the plan for this lesson.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• NETWORKDAYS: working days between two dates
• WORKDAY: a date some working days away
• A 2026 holiday list as a named range
• Six-day weeks with the .INTL versions
Practice sheet: S06-05

steps.say: NETWORKDAYS counts working days between two dates, including both ends. WORKDAY starts from a date and counts forward. The dot INTL versions add a weekend code.

acts.t:
NETWORKDAYS(start_date, end_date, [holidays])
WORKDAY(start_date, days, [holidays])
NETWORKDAYS.INTL(start_date, end_date, [weekend], [holidays])
WORKDAY.INTL(start_date, days, [weekend], [holidays])

steps.say: First, the holiday list. Open the sheet Holidays 2026. It has the three national holidays, which have fixed dates, plus Christmas and four festivals with sample dates. Replace the samples with your company's official list. The dates are named Holidays.
Back on sheet S06-05, each purchase order has an order date and a promised date. Click D2.
Type equals NETWORKDAYS of B2, comma, C2, and press Return. That counts Monday to Friday between the two dates, including both ends: 9 days.

That count ignores holidays. Retype D2 with a third argument, the name Holidays, and fill down. Row 2 drops to 8, because Republic Day, the twenty-sixth of January, falls on a Monday inside that window.

acts.h: Select D2:D8 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Many Indian offices and factories work six days a week. NETWORKDAYS dot INTL takes a weekend code, and 11 means only Sunday is off. In E2, type it with B2, C2, 11 and Holidays, then fill down.

acts.h: Select E2:E8 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Here are the weekend codes you'll use most.

acts.t:
Weekend codes for the .INTL functions
1 = Saturday and Sunday (default)
11 = Sunday only
17 = Saturday only
7 = Friday and Saturday
Or a 7-digit string Monday to Sunday, 1 = off: "0000011"

steps.say: WORKDAY goes the other way. In G2, type equals WORKDAY of B2, the SLA in F2, and Holidays. Press Return and fill down to get each delivery date. The order date itself is not counted.

acts.h: Select G2:G8 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Look at PO-2605 in row 6. Seven working days from the twenty-eighth of September skips Gandhi Jayanti on Friday the second of October, so delivery is on Thursday the eighth of October.
Now change an input. PO-2601's SLA is renegotiated to ten working days. Type 10 in F2 and press Return. The delivery date moves to the fourth of February.
Here's a quick recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• NETWORKDAYS counts working days between dates, both ends included
• WORKDAY finds a date N working days ahead
• Always pass your holiday list; use .INTL with 11 for a six-day week

steps.say: Your turn. In column H, work out the delivery date for a six-day week, using WORKDAY dot INTL with weekend code 11 and the holiday list.

acts.t:
Challenge
In H2:H8, delivery date with only Sunday off.
Hint: WORKDAY.INTL(B2, F2, 11, Holidays)
Answer: sheet S06-05 Done

lessons.title: DATEDIF and YEARFRAC: age and tenure
learn: Age in years, months and days

steps.say: This HR sheet shows each employee's exact age in years, months and days, their service in years, an estimated gratuity, and their retirement date. Everything is calculated as on one date in K1.
Here's the plan for this lesson.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• DATEDIF for age in years, months and days
• YEARFRAC for service length in decimal years
• A gratuity estimate that needs 5 years of service
Practice sheet: S06-06

steps.say: DATEDIF counts complete units between two dates. The unit is a code in quotes. YEARFRAC returns the fraction of years between two dates, and basis 1 uses actual days.

acts.t:
DATEDIF(start_date, end_date, unit)
"Y" years   "M" months   "D" days
"YM" months after whole years   "MD" days after whole months
YEARFRAC(start_date, end_date, [basis])  basis 1 = actual days

steps.say: Open sheet S06-06. K1 holds the as-on date, the thirty-first of March 2026, the last day of FY 2025-26. A fixed date, rather than TODAY, keeps HR reports repeatable. Click E2.

Type equals DATEDIF, open bracket, B2, comma, dollar K dollar 1, comma, Y in quotes, and press Return. Excel doesn't suggest DATEDIF as you type, because it's an old function kept for compatibility, but it works. Suresh is 57 complete years old.
A common mistake is swapping the dates. Retype E2 with K1 first and B2 second, and press Return. You get the NUM error, because the start date must come before the end date.
Now build the full age. Start again in E2 with DATEDIF of B2 and K1 in years, then an ampersand and space y space in quotes, and another ampersand.
Add DATEDIF with YM, which gives the months left over after whole years, then space m space in quotes and an ampersand.

Finish with MD, the days left over after whole months, and space d in quotes. Press Return and fill down. Suresh is 57 years, 8 months and 19 days old. Microsoft notes MD can be off around month ends, so check those cases.

acts.h: Select E2:E9 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Service for gratuity needs a decimal. In F2, type ROUND of YEARFRAC of the joining date C2 and K1, with basis 1 for actual days, to 2 decimals. Fill down. Suresh has 21.83 years of service.

acts.h: Select F2:F9 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Here's the gratuity rule we'll use, simplified from the Payment of Gratuity Act.

acts.t:
Gratuity estimate (simplified)
Eligible after 5 years of continuous service
Amount = last Basic + DA x 15/26 x completed years
A part-year over 6 months counts as a full year
Maximum ₹20 lakh. Check your company policy for edge cases.

steps.say: In G2, type equals IF, open bracket, F2 greater than or equal to 5, comma. Only people with five years or more get an amount.
Then ROUND of D2 times 15 divided by 26, times ROUND of F2 to whole years, rounded to whole rupees, and zero for everyone else. Press Return and fill down.

acts.h: Select G2:G9 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Yasmin in row 9 has 4.96 years of service, just under five, so her gratuity is zero for now.
Move the as-on date forward a month. Type 2026-04-30 in K1 and press Return. Ages and service update for everyone, and Yasmin crosses five years, so a gratuity amount appears.
Here's a quick recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• DATEDIF(start, end, "Y") for completed years; start must be earlier
• Join Y, YM and MD for an exact age
• ROUND(YEARFRAC(start, end, 1), 2) for service in years

steps.say: Your turn. In column H, find each employee's retirement date at sixty, on the last day of the month they turn sixty.

acts.t:
Challenge
In H2:H9, retirement at 60 on the last day of that month.
Hint: EOMONTH(EDATE(B2, 720), 0)
Answer: sheet S06-06 Done

lessons.title: Financial year and quarter formulas (April to March)
learn: Q1 to Q4 on the Indian calendar

steps.say: Every invoice here is labelled with its Indian financial year, like FY 2026-27, and its quarter from Q1 to Q4 on the April to March calendar. You'll use these labels in every GST, tax and board report.
Here's the plan for this lesson.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• An FY label from any date
• Q1 to Q4 on the April to March calendar
• The TRUE = 1 trick for date logic
Practice sheet: S06-07

steps.say: The Indian financial year runs from the first of April to the thirty-first of March. A date in January, February or March belongs to the year that started the previous April.

acts.t:
Indian financial year: 1 April to 31 March
FY 2026-27 = 01-04-2026 to 31-03-2027
Q1 Apr-Jun   Q2 Jul-Sep   Q3 Oct-Dec   Q4 Jan-Mar

steps.say: Here's the trick. MONTH less than 4 is TRUE for January to March, and TRUE counts as 1. So the year minus that test is the year the financial year started.
Open sheet S06-07. There are ten invoices from January 2026 to March 2027. Click C2.
Type equals, FY and a space in quotes, ampersand, then in brackets YEAR of B2 minus, in brackets, MONTH of B2 less than 4. For the fifteenth of January 2026 that's 2026 minus 1, which is 2025.
Add a dash in quotes, then the next year's last two digits: RIGHT of the same start year plus 1, comma, 2. Press Return. You get FY 2025-26.
Fill down. The thirty-first of March 2026 is still FY 2025-26, and the first of April 2026 starts FY 2026-27.

acts.h: Select C2:C11 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: For quarters, many people use the calendar formula: ROUNDUP of MONTH divided by 3. Type it in D2 with Q in front and fill down. January shows Q1, but in India's financial year it's Q4.

acts.h: Select D2:D11 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Shift the months so April counts as zero: MONTH minus 4. MOD with 12 wraps January, February and March round to 9, 10 and 11. Divide by 3, drop the decimals with INT, and add 1.

acts.t:
Quarter on the Indian FY
="Q"&(INT(MOD(MONTH(B2)-4,12)/3)+1)
April: MOD(0,12)=0, so Q1
January: MOD(-3,12)=9, 9/3=3, so Q4

steps.say: Retype D2 with this formula and fill down. January is now Q4, April Q1, July Q2 and October Q3.

acts.h: Select D2:D11 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: If you prefer something easier to read, CHOOSE works too.

acts.t:
Alternative
="Q"&CHOOSE(MONTH(B2),4,4,4,1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3)
One quarter number for each month, January to December

steps.say: Change an input to test the boundary. In B11, type 2027-04-05 and press Return. The label moves to FY 2027-28, quarter Q1.
Here's a quick recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• FY start year = YEAR(date) - (MONTH(date)<4)
• FY label: "FY " & start & "-" & RIGHT(start+1, 2)
• FY quarter: INT(MOD(MONTH(date)-4,12)/3)+1

steps.say: Your turn. In column E, show the first day of each invoice's financial year as a real date, using DATE.

acts.t:
Challenge
In E2:E11, the FY start date, e.g. 01-04-2025.
Hint: DATE(YEAR(B2)-(MONTH(B2)<4), 4, 1)
Answer: sheet S06-07 Done

lessons.title: Working with time: shifts and overtime
lessons.mac:
(Excel app on Mac)
Command + 1 opens Format Cells, where you can type [h]:mm under Custom.
In Excel for the web: Home > Number Format > More Number Formats.

steps.say: This shift log works out hours for every shift, including night shifts that cross midnight, the overtime above nine hours, decimal hours for payroll, and a weekly total that goes past twenty-four hours.
Here's the plan for this lesson.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Subtract times, even across midnight
• Overtime with MAX and TIME
• Decimal hours for payroll
• Totals over 24 hours with [h]:mm
Practice sheet: S06-08

steps.say: Times are fractions of a day. Out minus In gives the hours worked, as long as the shift ends on the same day. MOD with 1 handles shifts that cross midnight.

acts.t:
Hours worked = Out - In
Across midnight: MOD(Out - In, 1)
TIME(hours, minutes, seconds) builds a time
Decimal hours = time x 24
[h]:mm shows totals beyond 24 hours

steps.say: Open sheet S06-08. This is a two-day shift log, and some shifts run past midnight. Click E2.
Type equals D2 minus C2, press Return and fill down to E10. Day shifts look fine: Ramesh worked 9 hours on Monday.

acts.h: Select E2:E10 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Now look at rows 6, 7 and 10. Imtiaz started at ten at night and left at six in the morning, so Out minus In is negative. Excel can't show a negative time, so you see hash marks.
MOD with 1 keeps only the fraction of a day and wraps negative values round. Retype E2 as MOD of D2 minus C2, comma, 1, and fill down. Imtiaz's night shift is 8 hours.

acts.h: Select E2:E10 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Overtime is anything over nine hours. In F2, type MAX of zero and E2 minus TIME of 9, 0, 0. TIME builds a time from hours, minutes and seconds. Fill down. Ramesh has two and a half hours of overtime on Tuesday.

acts.h: Select F2:F10 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Payroll needs decimal hours. A day has 24 hours, so multiply the time by 24. In G2, type E2 times 24 and fill down. Eleven hours thirty minutes becomes 11.50.

acts.h: Select G2:G10 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: In E12, type SUM of E2 to E10 and press Return. It shows 12:30, which can't be right for nine shifts.
The h colon mm format resets every 24 hours, like a clock. The real total is 84 hours 30 minutes, and the clock format shows only the 12 hours 30 left after three full days.

With E12 selected, open the Number Format box on the Home tab and choose More Number Formats. Pick Custom, type square bracket h, close square bracket, colon, m m, and click OK. The total now reads 84:30.
F12 is already formatted that way. Type SUM of F2 to F10 there. Total overtime is 5 hours 30 minutes.
Change an input. Ramesh actually left at quarter to ten on Tuesday night. Type 21:45 in D3 and press Return. His hours, overtime and the weekly total all update.
One shortcut differs in the Mac app.

acts.t:
Mac corner (Excel app on Mac)
Command + 1 opens Format Cells, where you can type [h]:mm under Custom.
In Excel for the web: Home > Number Format > More Number Formats.

steps.say: Here's a quick recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• MOD(Out - In, 1) handles shifts across midnight
• MAX(0, hours - TIME(9,0,0)) gives overtime
• Multiply by 24 for decimal hours; use [h]:mm for totals

steps.say: Your turn. In column H, work out overtime pay at two hundred and fifty rupees an hour. Turn the overtime into decimal hours first.

acts.t:
Challenge
In H2:H10, overtime pay at ₹250 per hour.
Hint: F2 * 24 * 250
Answer: sheet S06-08 Done
